positioning.iv_note: IV estimated compressing from ~52% to ~50% on the IG-ratings gap-up. July options at ~50–52% IV remain the hedge vehicle for any re-entry position. A July $175 put at current IV would cost approximately $10–12 — appropriate hedge size for a new long above $185. If SPCX produces two consecutive closes above $185, the option play is a July $185/$165 put spread to define downside risk for the re-entry position.
positioning.short_interest: P/C estimated ~1.08 (down from 1.12 as IG ratings reduce the fundamental bear case). Borrow availability continuing to normalize post-IPO Day 11. The IG rating gap-up has permanently retired the 'unrated credit history' bear argument — all three agencies simultaneously confirming investment-grade status within days of the IPO is a permanent franchise quality floor. The remaining short thesis is: (1) 84x revenue valuation with net losses; (2) September 2 earnings uncertainty; (3) December 9 lock-up expiry supply overhang. None of these three are affected by IG ratings. The short thesis is intact on valuation — the structural bear argument has narrowed from 'speculative credit + high multiple' to 'just high multiple.'

84x revenue multiple unchanged at $185 — IG ratings lower the cost of capital but they don't lower the revenue multiple; at $185 and $2.54T market cap, SPCX still requires Starlink growing >40% annually to September 2 earnings plus Starship recurring revenue plus Cursor AI contribution to justify the valuation; none of those fundamentals were disclosed in the rating agencies' assessments.

December 9 lock-up expiry is 170 days away — any investor who buys at $185 must be comfortable holding through the first major float expansion; lock-up expiry typically creates selling pressure 30–60 days before the event; the 84x multiple with approaching lock-up creates a ceiling on the re-rating until September 2 earnings reveals the disclosed financial picture.

MSCI passive bid exhausting (Day 11+) — the MSCI systematic rebalancing buying window that supported Days 1–10 post-IPO is largely exhausted; the volume needed to sustain >$185 (ideally >100M shares daily close volume) must come from genuine institutional conviction, not passive mechanics; IG ratings help, but the July expiry OI structure is the arbiter.
